explainer: The single best AI-bubble bellwether is the rental price of an installed Nvidia GPU, measured in dollars per GPU-hour, and specifically the H100: it is the daily marginal clearing price for AI compute, it is published by independent indexes (Silicon Data's SDH100RT, SemiAnalysis's one-year contract index), and a CME futures contract on it is pending: the CFTC extended its review to November 9, 2026, so a forward curve is coming but not yet listed. Right now it is saying the opposite of discounting: the Silicon Data index sits at $2.75/hr (Sep 30), a new high, one-year contract rates rose about 40% from $1.70 to $2.35 between October 2025 and March 2026, spot has run at roughly twice contract, and a four-year-old chip is renting for more than it did a year ago while CoreWeave says it has contracted 2020-vintage GPUs out to 2029 at full price. Pair it with three things: neocloud credit spreads (CoreWeave's July loan cleared at SOFR+550 for a 10.44% yield with maintenance covenants, and its CDS implies roughly a coin-flip default probability), which is the financing leg and the one signal already flashing red; server DRAM and HBM contract-price momentum (+13-18% QoQ in 3Q26 after +93-98% in 1Q26, with 4Q26 guided to only +3-8%), because memory is the first physical input that will roll over; and hyperscaler backlog growth versus capex growth (Microsoft commercial RPO +84%, Oracle RPO +363%, roughly $2.4 trillion of committed cloud backlog against about $1 trillion of 2026 capex), because the bubble only deflates if the buyers stop signing. Over the next one to two quarters watch Nvidia's August 26 print for gross margin and customer concentration (three direct customers were already 54% of revenue), the shape of the CME H100/B200 curve if the CFTC clears it in November (a steep backwardation would be the first public forecast of discounting), whether 4Q26 memory contract talks and 2027 HBM4 pricing turn negative, and what ERCOT's December audit says about how much of Texas's 474 GW interconnection queue is phantom demand. The threshold that would flip the call is simple: the H100 index sustained below about $2.00/hr, or spot trading below the one-year contract rate, while Blackwell and Rubin volumes keep arriving; until then compute is being sold at a premium, not a discount, and the risk lives in who is borrowing to build it rather than in the price of the product.

indicators.name: H100 rental price, $/GPU-hour (Silicon Data index; 1-yr contract and spot)
indicators.value: Silicon Data SDH100RT $2.85/hr as of Oct 9 (+2.5% 7d), up from $2.80 Oct 8 and $2.81 Oct 7. H200 $3.39 (+1.2% 7d), MI300X $2.64 (+0.4%), A100 $1.53 (+0.6%). CME H100 futures: still no confirmed listing date on Silicon Data's page; CFTC review status could not be re-verified Oct 8-10.
indicators.why: Hopper spot firmed through the Oct 8 OpenAI revenue scare: every Silicon Data index rose over the week, so rented compute is still being bid, not discounted.
indicators.watch: Bearish flip if SDH100RT prints below ~$2.00 for a month or spot drops under the 1-yr contract rate. Next: whether the Oct 8 demand scare shows up in the index with a lag, and the CME/CFTC listing decision.
indicators.note: Changed since Oct 8: the headline index rose 5c to $2.85 (Oct 9 reading) and the 7-day change widened to +2.5% from +1.1%; H200 rose 7c to $3.39 and A100 1c to $1.53. MI300X was unchanged at $2.64. The page's FAQ still quotes a stale $2.53 figure, which is ignored in favour of the dated headline reading. Silicon Data's own futures post (dated Jul 17) says no GPU futures contract has final CFTC approval and lists no launch date; the earlier note of a CFTC review window to Nov 9 could not be re-checked because web search was unavailable, so it is carried forward unverified. Inference: an index rising 2.5% in the same week the biggest buyer's revenue was marked down ~$20B says the rental market is pricing supply, not sentiment.

indicators.name: B200 rental price, $/GPU-hour (Silicon Data index) and B200/H100 ratio
indicators.value: Silicon Data B200 $5.93 Oct 9 (+1.2% 7d), up from $5.88 Oct 8; B300 $6.71 (+1.9% 7d) vs $6.69. B200/H100 ratio 2.08x (5.93/2.85), down from 2.10x only because Hopper rose faster. Both well above the $4.50 and 2x triggers.

indicators.watch: Bearish if B200 drops below $4.50 or the B200/H100 ratio falls under 2x. Also watch whether B300 keeps widening its premium over B200 as Rubin nears.

The ratio slipped from 2.10x to 2.08x; this is a Hopper-strength effect, not Blackwell weakness, since both numerator and denominator rose. The B200 page FAQ shows a stale $5.45, ignored. No B200-specific futures listing date appears on Silicon Data's futures post; the parent's note of a CME B200 contract pending CFTC review is carried forward. Nothing on the page has moved toward either trigger.

indicators.name: Hopper residual value: A100 index floor, used H100 prices, GPU useful-life accounting
indicators.value: A100 index $1.53 Oct 9 (+0.6% 7d; trigger $1.50) vs $1.52 Oct 8. Silicon Data residual study (Jan 30, 2026 data): used H100 ~65-75% of new at 2 yrs, 45-55% at 3 yrs; refurbished 80-90% / 70-75%; median resale mid-$20Ks late-2025, low end $12-16K. No new Hopper impairments or useful-life changes seen Oct 8-10.
indicators.why: A100 is still a cent or three above the $1.50 floor and ticked up this week; the residual-value question is unresolved rather than deteriorating.
indicators.watch: A100 index under $1.50; any hyperscaler or neocloud shortening GPU useful life or booking a Hopper impairment in Q3 results (late Oct onward); used H100 SXM asks drifting below $18K.
indicators.note: Changed since Oct 8: A100 +1c to $1.53, so the floor held. No new used-H100 price reports, useful-life changes or impairments were found: Nvidia's newsroom, The Register and TechCrunch carried none for Oct 8-10, and web search was unavailable for a targeted sweep, so the $18-27K used H100 SXM range, 3-4 yr lender underwriting and the Amazon ~$8B Grace Blackwell SPV are carried forward unchanged. Silicon Data's residual study is listing-price based and dated Jan 30, so it is context, not a fresh print. Inference: the OpenAI revenue revision is more relevant to this indicator than any GPU print this week, because a weaker anchor tenant is the main path to Hopper fleets being re-priced. Signal held at bullish: the observable reading (A100 rental) rose and no used-GPU print or impairment appeared; the OpenAI revenue point is a watch item, not a residual-value print.

indicators.watch: 10-yr back above 5.30%; any new campus announcement implying more than ~$60B/GW; Amazon's newly disclosed data-centre deal terms now that it is dropping NDAs.
indicators.note: Changed since Oct 8: the Treasury par-curve 10-yr closed 5.24% Oct 9 after 5.22% Oct 8, versus 5.28% Oct 7. The prior entry's 5.365% for Oct 7 does not match the Treasury par curve (5.28%); inference: it was an intraday or benchmark-note quote from another source, so the official par series is used from here. Nvidia's Oct 8 $1B five-year US science computing pledge (seven AI supercomputers) is small relative to campus budgets. Watch for the Oct 14 Anthropic session and Q3 hyperscaler capex updates for new $/GW anchors.

indicators.name: Memory prices: DRAM spot and contract, HBM, Samsung and Micron readthrough
indicators.value: TrendForce spot Oct 9: DDR5 16Gb $58.90 (+0.4% d/d, vs $58.40 Oct 7), DDR4 16Gb $83.64 (flat, vs $83.59), DDR4 8Gb $46.19 (-0.5%). Samsung Q3 prelim op profit W107.3-107.5T (~$80B, ~8.8x YoY) on revenue W194-196T. TrendForce: 4Q26 conventional DRAM contract +10-15% QoQ; 2027 blended HBM+DRAM ASP +121%. Global PC shipments -20% in Q3 on memory-driven prices.
indicators.why: Spot DRAM kept inching up through the AI selloff and Samsung's preliminary profit confirms the pricing power; the only soft spot is demand destruction in PCs, which does not touch server DRAM or HBM.
indicators.watch: TrendForce's October contract-price update (the contract table is still 2H Aug); Samsung full Q3 results late Oct; any sign DDR4 16Gb spot rolls over from $83-84; MU move after the Oct 8 chip selloff.
indicators.note: Changed since Oct 8: DDR5 16Gb spot +50c to $58.90 and DDR4 16Gb +5c to $83.64 (Oct 9 session), both new highs for this series; DDR4 8Gb eased slightly. The Register (Oct 8) puts Samsung's preliminary Q3 operating profit at W107.3-107.5T, about $80B, 8.8x last year, consistent with the 107.4T already recorded, and notes Samsung has warned the memory crunch could deepen in 2027 and persist into 2028. TrendForce's press centre had no new DRAM, HBM or contract-price releases Oct 6-10; its Oct 8 note forecasts low-single-digit notebook shipment declines in 2027 because of component costs, and The Register (Oct 9) reports Q3 global PC shipments down 20%. MU fell about 0.7% Friday after a larger Thursday drop in the chip selloff (the two-day move was about -5.4% per the parent's data); Yahoo's MU feed carried no new pricing news. Unchanged: TrendForce contract table (2H Aug), the 4Q26 +10-15% and 2027 +121% forecasts (Sep 29-30).

indicators.name: Power bottleneck: ERCOT/PJM queues, Texas permit freeze, turbine backlog
indicators.value: No new Texas prints Oct 8-10: ERCOT 474 GW large-load queue, TCEQ permit freeze since Sep 21 and the Oct 19 compliance report carried forward. PJM Oct 8 accepted the first 3 projects into its expedited interconnection track for large generation; Oct 9 issued a capacity advisory for Oct 12-13 on warm weather. GE Vernova 116 GW gas backlog unchanged.
indicators.why: Grid capacity is still the binding constraint on how fast compute can be deployed: PJM is issuing tight-conditions advisories in October and only just fast-tracking its first new generators, which keeps existing GPU capacity scarce.
indicators.watch: Texas TCEQ compliance report Oct 19; ERCOT Batch Zero timing; FERC action on PJM's large-load curtailment proposal; GE Vernova Q3 backlog (late Oct).
indicators.note: Changed since Oct 8: two PJM items. On Oct 8 PJM accepted the first three projects into its temporary expedited interconnection track, a process meant to bring large generation online quickly; this is the first concrete step on the supply side, but three projects against a multi-year queue is small. On Oct 9 PJM issued a capacity advisory for Oct 12-13 citing tight conditions from warm weather, notable for a shoulder-season week. Not refreshed: ERCOT's news pages returned 404/403 and web search was unavailable, so the 474 GW queue, TCEQ freeze, Oracle Jupiter force majeure and the Senate's 57-43 vote on the Ratepayer Protection Act are carried forward unchanged. Nothing new on turbine backlogs Oct 8-10. Next hard date is the Oct 19 TCEQ compliance report.

indicators.name: Capex vs backlog: hyperscaler spend, RPO, AI-lab commitments and buyer revenue quality
indicators.value: OpenAI told investors annualised revenue is 'approaching $50B' (FT via TechCrunch Oct 8) vs ~$70B assumed since a late-Sep Axios report; the gap is methodology (Anthropic counts cloud-partner sales, OpenAI does not). OpenAI IPO pushed to early 2027. Anthropic $518B commitments (investor session Oct 14), Oracle RPO $664B, Amazon ~$220B 2026 capex, Micron ~$150B RPO unchanged.
indicators.why: The commitments did not change but the biggest buyer's revenue base is ~30% smaller than the market assumed, so backlog coverage by customer revenue got worse on paper; it is an accounting gap, not a demand drop, which keeps this neutral rather than bearish.
indicators.watch: Anthropic investor session Oct 14; OpenAI's $30B round at $1.4T pre-money closing or re-priced; Q3 hyperscaler capex guides late Oct; whether Bloomberg's reported $70B+ year-end run-rate is confirmed by OpenAI.
indicators.note: Changed since Oct 8: this is the week's key datapoint. TechCrunch (Oct 8) reports the FT's figure that OpenAI's annualised revenue is approaching $50B against roughly $70B investors had assumed, with the difference explained by OpenAI excluding partner-channel sales that Anthropic includes; the same piece notes OpenAI's IPO has slipped to early 2027 and that 2025 revenue was about $13B. The parent's context adds that Bloomberg (Oct 9) said OpenAI expects $70B+ annualised by year-end and that the $30B round remains in talks; neither could be opened directly. Market read: chipmakers fell about 3.4% Thursday and CoreWeave 7.8%, Friday's bounce faded by the close. Also Oct 9: TechCrunch reports Amazon is dropping NDAs on data-centre deals, and Anthropic said it cannot reliably control its agents and is cutting internal evals off from the live internet. Unchanged: Oracle, Amazon, Micron, Marvell and Goldman's $1.4T 2027 capex figures. Inference: the backlog numbers on this page are only as good as the revenue of the labs behind them, and this week that revenue was restated, not the backlog.

Nothing found on Nebius, Lambda or Crusoe financing or on Broadcom's OpenAI debt talks Oct 8-10; those remain open items. Inference: a 7.8% equity drop on a customer accounting revision implies the 2031s widened further, but no quote was observed. Waymo's $5B term loan (parent context) shows AI-adjacent debt is still available for non-GPU borrowers. Signal held at neutral, as on Oct 8: an equity drop is not a credit print, and the bearish flip waits for a bond, loan or CDS quote through the 11% line.

indicators.name: Nvidia data centre: revenue, margin, concentration, backstops and demand signals

Oct 8: $1B five-year US science compute pledge; a director sold $947M of stock last quarter. DC rev $89.0B (+117%), GM 75.0%, Q3 guide $108B, $150B buyback, $500B chip-collateral plan, GTC DC Nov 30-Dec 3 unchanged. No China/export news.

indicators.watch: Anthropic investor session Oct 14; any OpenAI round re-pricing; GTC Washington Nov 30-Dec 3; Q3 FY27 results in late Nov (inference from prior cadence); CFTC/CME GPU futures listing.
indicators.note: Changed since Oct 8: NVDA fell about 2.9% Thursday and a further 0.5% Friday (Yahoo close data), so the two-day move was about -3.4% and the Friday intraday bounce on Bloomberg's $70B+ OpenAI year-end report did not hold into the close. Nvidia's newsroom shows one press release in the window: Oct 8, $1B over five years for US scientific computing; The Register adds seven AI-optimised supercomputers. Yahoo's feed flags a director's $947M of sales last quarter and a Sequoia-backed chip startup (Nuvacore) seeking a $2.5B valuation; neither changes the demand picture. Inference: with the OpenAI programme reportedly backed by up to $105B of Nvidia money, OpenAI's revenue methodology now matters as much as Nvidia's own numbers for how the market treats the backstop. Signal unchanged: nothing this week showed discounting at the source (margin, guide and buyback all stand); the two-day share drop is sentiment about a customer's accounting, so trend stays with the operating numbers.
